entries.content_plain: PSALM 126 Psa 126:1-6 . To praise for God's favor to His people is added a prayer for its continued manifestation. 1-3. All did not return at once; hence the prayer for repeated favors.<div eID="gen10766" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen10767" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">as the streams in the south--</hi>or, the torrents in the desert south of Judea, dependent on rain (<reference osisRef="Josh.15.9">Jos 15:9</reference>), reappearing after dry seasons (compare <reference osisRef="Job.6.15">Job 6:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.68.9">Psa 68:9</reference>). The point of comparison is joy at the reappearing of what has been so painfully missed. <div eID="gen10767" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 4. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7016"/><div sID="gen10768" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7016"/>5-6. As in husbandry the sower may cast his seed in a dry and parched soil with desponding fears, so those shall reap abundant fruit who toil in tears with the prayer of faith. (Compare the history, <reference osisRef="Ezra.6.16">Ezr 6:16</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezra.6.22">22</reference>). <div eID="gen10768" type="x-p"/>
